transcript: What's the best advice you can give to someone who constantly over-thinks everything? Overthinking is often the mind's attempt to create certainty where certainty does not exist. The mind says, if I think about this long enough, maybe I can control the outcome, maybe I can prevent pain, but life does not work that way. The more you chase certainty, the more anxious you become. So instead of fighting your thoughts, give them a place to rest. When a worry appears, write it down. Do not carry it with you all day. Simply say, I see you, I will return to you later. Then continue living your life. At the end of the day, spend 10 minutes with your worries. Read them, reflect on them. You will notice that many of the fears that felt so heavy in the morning have become much smaller, and many of them were never yours to control in the first place. The goal is not to stop thinking. The goal is to stop believing that every thought deserves your attention. Peace comes when you stop trying to control everything and start trusting yourself to handle whatever comes next. The mind wants certainty. But wisdom learns to live without it.
